alt: Yellow quote card: Don't wait for Monday. Start with your next meal.

quote: The best project you'll ever work on is you.
title: The Best Project You'll Ever Work On Is You (Self-Care Quote)
desc: A self-care reminder: the best project you'll ever work on is you. Healthy food, movement and good sleep are not punishments, they are an investment in yourself. #selfcare #weightlossmotivation #motivationalquotes
alt: Golden field at sunset with the quote: The best project you'll ever work on is you

quote: Eat well. Move daily. Sleep enough. Repeat.
title: Eat Well, Move Daily, Sleep Enough, Repeat: Simple Healthy Living
desc: Healthy living can be this simple: eat well, move every day, sleep enough and repeat. No crash diets, no extreme workouts, just good habits done consistently. #healthyliving #healthyhabits #weightlossmotivation
alt: Cream quote card: Eat well. Move daily. Sleep enough. Repeat.

quote: Be kind to yourself. You're doing better than you think.
title: Be Kind to Yourself, You're Doing Better Than You Think
desc: A gentle reminder for your weight loss journey: be kind to yourself, you're doing better than you think. Every healthy choice counts, even on the days that feel hard. #selflove #weightlossmotivation #motivationalquotes
alt: Calm blue lake at dawn with the quote: Be kind to yourself. You're doing better than you think

quote: Progress happens when you show up, even on the hard days.
title: Progress Happens When You Show Up, Even on the Hard Days
desc: Motivation comes and goes, habits stay. Progress happens when you show up, even on the hard days: a short walk, a simple healthy meal, an early night. That's how results are built. #weightlossmotivation #fitnessmotivation #healthyhabits
alt: Green quote card: Progress happens when you show up, even on the hard days.

quote: One healthy choice makes the next one easier.
title: One Healthy Choice Makes the Next One Easier (Motivation Quote)
desc: Healthy habits build on each other: one healthy choice makes the next one easier. A good breakfast, then a walk, then water instead of soda. Start with one today. #healthyhabits #weightlossmotivation #motivationalquotes
alt: Sunrise over a calm sea and an empty beach with the quote: One healthy choice makes the next one easier

quote: You are one walk away from a better mood.
title: You Are One Walk Away From a Better Mood (Motivation Quote)
desc: Feeling stressed or stuck? You are one walk away from a better mood. Even 10 minutes outside can clear your head. Put on your shoes and go. #walkingmotivation #selfcare #weightlossmotivation
alt: Yellow quote card: You are one walk away from a better mood.

quote: Fall in love with taking care of yourself.
title: Fall in Love With Taking Care of Yourself (Self-Care Quote)
desc: Self-care quote for your healthy lifestyle: fall in love with taking care of yourself. Nourishing food, daily movement and rest are acts of self-love, not punishment. #selfcare #selflove #weightlossmotivation
alt: Wildflowers in a meadow at sunset with the quote: Fall in love with taking care of yourself

quote: It's not a diet. It's a lifestyle.
title: It's Not a Diet, It's a Lifestyle: Healthy Weight Loss Mindset
desc: The mindset that makes weight loss last: it's not a diet, it's a lifestyle. Choose habits you can keep for years, not rules you can only follow for a few weeks. #healthylifestyle #weightlossmotivation #mindset
alt: Cream quote card: It's not a diet. It's a lifestyle.

headline: Do carbs make you gain weight?
fact: Eating more calories than you burn does. Oats, potatoes, fruit and whole grains fit into a weight loss plan.
title: Myth vs. Fact: Do Carbs Make You Gain Weight?
desc: Myth: carbs make you gain weight. Fact: eating more calories than you burn does. Oats, potatoes, fruit and whole grains can absolutely fit into a healthy weight loss plan. #weightlossmyths #healthyeating #carbs
alt: Myth vs. fact card about carbs and weight gain

headline: Can crunches burn belly fat?
fact: You can't burn fat from one spot. A calorie deficit, strength training and daily walks reduce fat everywhere, including your belly.
title: Myth vs. Fact: Can Crunches Burn Belly Fat?
desc: Myth: crunches burn belly fat. Fact: you can't burn fat from one spot. A calorie deficit, strength training and daily walks reduce fat all over your body, including your belly. #bellyfat #weightlossmyths #fitnesstips
alt: Myth vs. fact card about crunches and belly fat

headline: Does eating late make you gain weight?
myth: Eating after 8 pm makes you gain weight.
fact: How much you eat over the whole day matters more than the clock. Late-night snacks are often just extra calories.
title: Myth vs. Fact: Does Eating After 8 PM Make You Gain Weight?
desc: Myth: eating after 8 pm makes you gain weight. Fact: how much you eat over the whole day matters more than the clock. The problem is that late-night snacks are often extra calories on top. #weightlossmyths #latenightsnacking #weightlosstips
alt: Myth vs. fact card about eating late at night

headline: Do you have to give up sweets?
myth: You have to cut out all sweets to lose weight.
fact: A small treat can fit into a healthy plan. Strict bans often end in overeating.
title: Myth vs. Fact: Do You Have to Give Up Sweets to Lose Weight?
desc: Myth: you have to cut out all sweets to lose weight. Fact: a small treat can fit into a healthy plan. Strict food bans often end in overeating. Enjoy a little, mindfully. #weightlossmyths #healthybalance #sugarcravings
alt: Myth vs. fact card about sweets and weight loss

headline: Does skipping meals help?
myth: Skipping meals helps you lose weight faster.
fact: It often makes you so hungry that you overeat later. Regular meals with protein keep hunger in check.
title: Myth vs. Fact: Does Skipping Meals Help You Lose Weight?
desc: Myth: skipping meals helps you lose weight faster. Fact: it often makes you so hungry that you overeat later. Regular meals with protein and fiber keep your hunger in check. #weightlossmyths #healthyeating #weightlosstips
alt: Myth vs. fact card about skipping meals

headline: Is fat-free food always better?
myth: Fat-free food is always the healthier choice.
fact: Many fat-free products have extra sugar or starch. Check the label for calories and sugar.
title: Myth vs. Fact: Is Fat-Free Food Always Healthier?
desc: Myth: fat-free food is always the healthier choice. Fact: many fat-free products contain extra sugar or starch to make up for the taste. Check the label for calories and sugar. #weightlossmyths #foodlabels #healthyeating
alt: Myth vs. fact card about fat-free food

headline: Do you need hours at the gym?
myth: You need to work out for hours to lose weight.
fact: Your diet matters most for weight loss. 30 minutes of movement a day is great for your health and helps you keep the weight off.
title: Myth vs. Fact: Do You Need Hours at the Gym to Lose Weight?
desc: Myth: you need to work out for hours to lose weight. Fact: your diet matters most for weight loss. About 30 minutes of movement a day is great for your health and helps you keep the weight off. #weightlossmyths #fitnessforbeginners #weightlosstips
alt: Myth vs. fact card about exercise and weight loss

headline: Is healthy food expensive?
fact: Oats, eggs, beans, lentils, frozen vegetables and seasonal fruit are some of the cheapest foods you can buy.
title: Myth vs. Fact: Is Healthy Food Expensive?
desc: Myth: eating healthy is always expensive. Fact: oats, eggs, beans, lentils, frozen vegetables and seasonal fruit are some of the cheapest foods you can buy. Healthy eating on a budget is possible. #budgetmeals #healthyeating #weightlossmyths
alt: Myth vs. fact card about the cost of healthy food

headline: Craving something crunchy?
why: Same crunch, a bigger bowl and more fiber.
title: Healthy Swap: Air-Popped Popcorn Instead of Chips
desc: Craving something crunchy? Swap 30 g of potato chips (about 160 kcal) for 3 cups of air-popped popcorn (about 95 kcal). Same crunch, a bigger bowl and more fiber. #healthyswaps #healthysnacks #lowcaloriesnacks
alt: Potato chips next to a bowl of popcorn as a healthy snack swap

headline: Thirsty for something fizzy?
why: Swap one can a day and save about 1,000 kcal a week.
title: Healthy Swap: Sparkling Water With Lemon Instead of Soda
desc: Swap a can of cola (about 140 kcal) for sparkling water with lemon (almost 0 kcal). One can a day adds up to about 1,000 kcal a week. Same fizz, no sugar. #healthyswaps #lowcaloriedrinks #weightlosstips
alt: Glass of cola next to a jar of water with lemon slices as a healthy drink swap

headline: Love fries?
why: Crispy from the oven with paprika and herbs, and just a little oil.
title: Healthy Swap: Oven Potato Wedges Instead of Fries
desc: Love fries? Swap a medium serving of deep-fried fries (about 350 kcal) for oven-baked potato wedges with 1 tsp of oil, paprika and herbs (about 160 kcal). Crispy, filling and much lighter. #healthyswaps #healthyrecipes #weightloss
alt: French fries next to oven-baked potato wedges with herbs as a healthy swap

headline: Chocolate craving?
why: You still get the chocolate, plus fruit that fills you up.
title: Healthy Swap for Chocolate Cravings: Strawberries + Dark Chocolate
desc: Chocolate craving? Instead of half a bar of milk chocolate (about 270 kcal), have a bowl of strawberries with one square of dark chocolate (about 110 kcal). You still get the chocolate, plus fruit that fills you up. #healthyswaps #chocolatecravings #healthydessert
alt: Milk chocolate bar next to strawberries with dark chocolate as a healthy swap

headline: Sweet tooth in the morning?
why: Sweet and creamy, with protein that keeps you full until lunch.
title: Healthy Breakfast Swap: Greek Yogurt With Berries Instead of a Donut
desc: Sweet tooth in the morning? Swap a frosted donut (about 270 kcal) for plain Greek yogurt with berries (about 130 kcal). Sweet, creamy and full of protein that keeps you full until lunch. #healthyswaps #healthybreakfast #highprotein
alt: Frosted donuts next to a bowl of Greek yogurt with berries as a breakfast swap

headline: Want something cold and sweet?
why: Blend them with a splash of milk for an instant sorbet.
title: Healthy Dessert Swap: Frozen Berries Instead of Ice Cream
desc: Want something cold and sweet? Swap a cup of ice cream (about 270 kcal) for a cup of frozen berries (about 70 kcal). Blend them with a splash of milk for an instant sorbet. #healthyswaps #healthydessert #lowcalorie
alt: Ice cream scoops next to a tray of frozen berries as a healthy dessert swap

headline: Craving candy?
why: Sweet, juicy and fun to snack on. Try them frozen!
title: Healthy Swap: Grapes Instead of Candy (Try Them Frozen!)
desc: Craving candy? Swap 50 g of sour candy (about 170 kcal) for 150 g of grapes (about 105 kcal). Sweet, juicy and fun to snack on, with water and fiber. Tip: frozen grapes taste like little sorbet bites. #healthyswaps #healthysnacks #sugarcravings
alt: Colorful sour candy next to a plate of green grapes as a healthy snack swap

headline: Pasta night?
why: Same big bowl, half the pasta. You won't even miss it.
title: Healthy Pasta Swap: Half Pasta, Half Zucchini Noodles
desc: Pasta night without the guilt: instead of 2 cups of cooked pasta (about 440 kcal), mix 1 cup of pasta with zucchini noodles (about 240 kcal). Same big bowl, half the pasta, and you won't even miss it. #healthyswaps #zucchininoodles #healthydinner
alt: Bowl of creamy pasta next to zucchini noodles with pesto as a healthy swap

body: For example 2 eggs with 150 g of Greek yogurt, or 250 g of skyr with berries. It keeps you full until lunch.
title: Aim for 25–30 g of Protein at Breakfast to Stay Full Until Lunch
desc: A high-protein breakfast keeps you full until lunch. Aim for 25 to 30 g of protein, for example 2 eggs with 150 g of Greek yogurt or 250 g of skyr with berries. #highproteinbreakfast #protein #weightlosstips
alt: Brown eggs in a white egg tray next to a whisk

body: Studies link around 7,000 to 8,000 daily steps with better health. Start where you are and add 1,000 steps each week.
title: 8,000 Steps a Day: A Realistic Walking Goal for Health
desc: You don't need 10,000 steps: studies link around 7,000 to 8,000 steps a day with better health. Start where you are and add about 1,000 steps each week. #walkingforweightloss #stepgoal #fitnessforbeginners
alt: Pair of sneakers on a forest floor surrounded by ferns

body: That's about 6 to 8 glasses for most adults, more on hot days and when you exercise. Water and tea are best.
title: How Much Water Should You Drink? About 1.5–2 Liters a Day
desc: How much should you drink? Most adults need about 1.5 to 2 liters of fluids a day, that's 6 to 8 glasses, and more on hot days or when you exercise. Water and unsweetened tea are best. #drinkmorewater #hydration #healthyhabits
alt: Glass pitcher of lemon water and a vase of flowers on a wooden table

body: One portion is about a handful (80 g). Aim for 3 portions of vegetables and 2 of fruit.
unit: portions of fruit and veg a day
title: 5 Portions of Fruit and Vegetables a Day: What Counts?
desc: Aim for 5 portions of fruit and vegetables a day. One portion is about a handful (80 g). Try 3 portions of vegetables and 2 of fruit, and eat as many colors as you can. #eattherainbow #healthyeating #fruitsandvegetables
alt: Colorful slices of oranges, grapefruit, lemons and limes

body: That's just 30 minutes on 5 days. Brisk walking, cycling, dancing and swimming all count.
title: 150 Minutes of Activity a Week: The Simple Fitness Goal
desc: The recommended goal for adults is at least 150 minutes of moderate activity a week. That's just 30 minutes on 5 days, and brisk walking, cycling, dancing and swimming all count. #fitnessforbeginners #movemore #healthyhabits
alt: Old pink bicycle leaning against a white wooden wall on green grass

body: A daily deficit of about 500 kcal leads to roughly 0.5 kg (1 lb) of weight loss a week. No crash diet needed.
title: How to Lose 0.5 kg a Week: Eat About 500 Calories Less a Day
desc: The simple math of fat loss: a daily deficit of about 500 calories leads to roughly 0.5 kg (1 lb) of weight loss per week. Eat a little less and move a little more, no crash diet needed. #caloriedeficit #weightlosstips #weightlossjourney
alt: Plate with vegetables, grains and legumes surrounded by small bowls of healthy food
